title: Probing Low-Energy Reciprocal-Space Excitations in 2D Materials from Atomic Crystals to Nanophotonic Arrays Using Momentum- and Pseudoangular Momentum-Resolved EELS
content: Alongside the recent proliferation of 2D quantum and nanophotonic materials comes the companion need to develop new measurement techniques for their characterization at their natural response scales in energy, length, momentum, and pseudoangular momentum (PAM). Advances in monochromation and aberration-correction technologies in scanning transmission electron microscopes (STEMs) now enable the investigation of low-energy excitations through inelastic free electron scattering approaching 1 meV, 0.01 Å-1, and 1 nm energy, momentum, and spatial resolutions, via electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS). The broad objective of this talk will be to highlight recent work conducted in my group on the theoretical design of new classes of delocalized and localized electron probes endowed with precise symmetries to additionally characterize the PAM-dependence of collective excitations such as phonons, exciton polaritons, and lattice plasmon polaritons in 2D periodic quantum and nanophotonic materials exhibiting chiral and topological character [1-4].
